cost.one: Nothing. There is no paid tier, no advertising, nothing behind a login, and the <docs>api</docs> is open. <donate>Donations</donate> are the only thing keeping it that way, and the badges they carry are cosmetic.
cost.title: What it costs you
cost.two: What is held about an account, and how to make it stop, is on the <privacy>privacy page</privacy>. The opt-out is one switch and takes effect immediately. The <tos>terms</tos> say the rest. {name} is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by Twitch Interactive, Inc.

donated.one: Your donation still counts here. We decided to honor every donation made under the old name rather than start the ledger over, so the donator badge you earned then came across with the rest of the data and is on your profile now.
donated.title: If you donated back when it was modchecker
donated.two: That is the likely answer if you are wearing a badge on a site you don't remember giving anything to. There is nothing to claim and nothing to renew, and it doesn't expire. If you did donate back then and the badge isn't showing, say so in <discord>the Discord</discord> and it will be put right by hand.

about.heading: What {name} is, and who runs it

history.one: {name} started out under the name modchecker.com. In August 2026 the project separated from that domain and from its original owner, moved to {domain}, and was rebuilt along the way into four separate services.
history.three: Ownership, hosting, the domain, the database and the code now sit entirely with the person running this site. There is no shared control and no arrangement of any kind with the old domain or with anyone behind it. If you followed a modchecker link here, that is the whole of what changed.
history.title: It used to be modchecker.com
history.two: What changed hands was the name: the original owner held the domain and the Discord server. The database was never theirs. It has been on the same server, in the same hands, the whole way through, and it did not move for the rename.

about.lead: {name} records which Twitch accounts hold moderator, VIP or founder status in which channels, and the day they got it. Twitch shows a broadcaster their own list. {name} keeps the other half.
about.metaDescription: Who runs {domain}, where it came from, and what happened to donations made back when it was modchecker.com.

who.one: One person, and that is the whole team. The domain, the server, the database and the code all sit in the same pair of hands, and no part of {name} is operated by anybody else.
who.title: Who runs it
who.two: More about the person behind it at <author>maersux.dev</author>, and the code can be read at <github>github.com/moddextv</github>.

keys.heading: Bot keys
keys.blurb: A key raises a bot out of the shared per-address rate limit and lets it ask for a channel to be re-indexed. It buys throughput and that one request, never trust: a keyed bot still sees exactly what the public sees.
keys.label: Key name
keys.createFailed: The key could not be created.
keys.revokeFailed: The key could not be revoked.
keys.revokeBody: {label} stops working at once. Only the hash is stored, so the key can be neither read back nor restored.
keys.rotateFailed: The key could not be rotated.
keys.rotateBody: {label} gets a new secret and the old one stops working at once. Any client still sending the old key is refused until you enter the new one.
keys.shownOnce: Copy this now. It is shown once and cannot be read back.
keys.unreadable: The keys could not be read.

dashboard.signInBlurb: It's team only, so moddex has to know which Twitch account is yours before it can check.
dashboard.signInHeading: The dashboard needs a Twitch sign-in

donate.heading: {brandName} runs on one server and no advertising
donate.lead: No paid tier, nothing behind a login, and the api is open. Donations are the only thing keeping it that way.
donate.metaDescription: {brandName} runs on one server and no advertising. No paid tier, nothing behind a login, and the api is open.
donate.signedOut: Sign in with Twitch first and the badge lands on your profile automatically. Donating signed out works too, it just needs a message in the Discord afterward.

straight.one: A contribution to running costs, not a purchase.
straight.three: Generally non-refundable. If something went wrong, write and we'll sort it out.
straight.title: Being straight about it
straight.two: The badges are cosmetic. They don't unlock anything and carry no monetary value.

donate.stripeNote: {brandName} stores the payment reference and the amount, nothing else. Stripe handles the card details end to end.
donate.stripeUnreachable: We couldn't reach Stripe, so nothing was charged. Try again in a moment.

banned.body: Twitch isn't serving this account, so {brandName} won't serve a profile for it either. Any roles it held stay in the index, just hidden for as long as this lasts.
banned.reversible: Bans get reversed sometimes, which is why this is the only state on the site that offers to read again.
banned.unrecognized: We show you whatever Twitch said, even when we don't recognize it.

checkout.body: {brandName} couldn't read the checkout session back from Stripe, so it can't show you a summary. None of that touches the donation itself.
checkout.byHand: If the badge is still missing an hour from now, send us the Stripe receipt and we'll assign it by hand.
checkout.heading: Your payment is fine. This page isn't.

invalid.body: Twitch names run 1 to 25 characters and allow only letters, numbers and underscores. That one can't exist, so we never asked Twitch about it.
invalid.heading: <name>{username}</name> can't be a Twitch name

errors.keepsHappening: If it keeps happening, <status>{host}</status> shows whether the api is up. It runs on separate infrastructure, so it stays up when this does not.
errors.listUnread: We couldn't read the index for this list.

notFound.body: We asked Twitch and it has no account by that name, so there was nothing to index. People rename themselves a lot, so check the spelling and try again.
notFound.heading: There's no Twitch account called <name>{username}</name>

errors.otherListsFine: The other lists on this page are unaffected.
errors.renderFailed: Something broke while the page was rendering, and we've logged it. Retrying rebuilds just this part of the page, which usually works if it was a slow response and not a real bug.

signIn.body: Twitch sent you back, but {brandName} could not finish the sign-in, so you are not signed in. Nothing was written here and nothing changed on your Twitch account. A sign-in left half finished for too long expires, which is the ordinary cause, and starting it again clears it.
signIn.deniedBody: Twitch asked whether {brandName} may see which account is yours, and the answer was no. Nothing was handed over and nothing was saved. Everything on this site except your own settings works signed out.
signIn.heading: That sign-in did not finish

unknownPage.body: That address doesn't lead anywhere on this site, so nothing was looked up. Everywhere worth going from here is below.

channel.disconnectBody: Mod and VIP changes stop reaching moddex as they happen. Nothing already recorded is lost, and the channel keeps being read on the normal schedule. Reconnecting means going through Twitch again.
channel.live: Mod and VIP changes reach {brandName} as they happen. Founders still come from the normal read, because Twitch has no live event for those. Withdrawing changes nothing that is already recorded.
channel.noToken: {brandName} posts nothing and keeps no token, so we read the list of channels you moderate once, right now, and it goes stale from then on. Reconnect to refresh it. You can withdraw at Twitch or here whenever you want.
channel.pitch: Two things at once. Mod and VIP changes in your channel reach {brandName} as they happen instead of on the next sweep. And the channels <you>you</you> moderate get filled in straight from Twitch, including ones nobody has ever looked up here.

channelStatus.connected: Channel connected. Moderator and VIP changes now reach moddex as they happen.
channelStatus.connected-nosync: Channel connected, but we couldn't save the list of channels you moderate. Live updates are working. Reconnect later to add the list.
channelStatus.exchange: Twitch didn't confirm the authorization. Try again.
channelStatus.failed: Something went wrong while saving, and your settings are unchanged. Try again in a moment.
channelStatus.mismatch: You approved that on Twitch as a different account from the one you're signed in with here, so we refused the connection.
channelStatus.nocode: Twitch sent back no authorization. Try again.
channelStatus.scopes: Twitch withheld one of the two permissions. We need both for moderator and VIP events, so the channel stayed disconnected.
channelStatus.signin: Your session ended before this finished. Sign in and try again.
channelStatus.state: That link expired or didn't belong to this session. Start again from the button above.

settings.discordRemoveBody: Your Twitch and Discord accounts stop being linked. Any Discord role moddex grants from a badge, booster included, comes off at the next sync. Linking again means going through Discord once more.

discordStatus.canceled: Canceled. No Discord account was linked.
discordStatus.connected: Discord connected. It now shows on your public profile.
discordStatus.exchange: Discord didn't confirm the account. Try again.
discordStatus.failed: Something went wrong while saving, and your profile is unchanged. Try again in a moment.
discordStatus.nocode: Discord sent back no authorization. Try again.
discordStatus.signin: Your session ended before this finished. Sign in and try again.
discordStatus.state: That link expired or didn't belong to this session. Start again from the button above.
discordStatus.taken: That Discord account is already connected to another moddex profile. Disconnect it there first.
discordStatus.unconfigured: Discord connections aren't set up on this server yet.
